sentences.text: This dinosaur displayed classic sauropod traits, such as a lengthy neck, a diminutive head, a long tail, and a four-legged posture.
Estimates suggest the animal reached a total length of 16.5 meters and a mass of roughly 7.88 metric tons.
Analysis of the adult lower jaws indicates the creature likely possessed a snout that was short, tall, and broad.
A well-preserved sacrum reveals that the skeleton included five vertebrae in this central region.
The pelvic structure featured ischia that were notably slender compared to the pubis, with only a minor widening at the distal end.
Histological research shows the animal replaced its teeth every 58 days.
Its unique tooth shape allowed it to avoid competing directly with other sauropods by occupying a different dietary niche.
Scientists propose that thinner enamel on its teeth was an adaptation for eating vegetation containing high levels of abrasive material.
Fossils were first uncovered in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, a rock unit dating to approximately 178 million years ago.
José Bonaparte formally named and described the genus in 1979.
Excavations in the 1970s also yielded many remains of an unidentified dinosaur from the same geological layer and location.
The presence of numerous specimens, including at least one juvenile, provides a clear picture of its anatomy and development.
Young individuals showed distinct differences from adults in the jaw, shoulder girdle, pelvis, and hind legs.
In mature adults, the pubic bones were significantly larger and sturdier than in the younger stages.
The fourth trochanter on the femur of the juvenile was situated entirely at the upper end of the bone.
The surrounding flora consisted mainly of conifers, though ferns and horsetails were also plentiful.
A layer of ash found directly beneath the formation suggests the area was near an active volcano.
A study published in 2021 placed the animal within the family Cetiosauridae.
Phylogenetic work from 2020, 2021, and 2024 confirmed a close evolutionary link between this genus, Bagualia, Nebulasaurus, and Spinophorosaurus.

It shares characteristics with related groups like Cetiosaurus and Volkheimeria, as well as primitive forms such as Barapasaurus and Amygdalodon, and derived sauropods like Diplodocus and Camarasaurus.
While some researchers, including Bonaparte and Upchurch, assign it to Cetiosauridae, this placement remains a subject of discussion.
The creature lived during the Middle Toarcian period.
Its habitat was a hypersaline and alkaline lake environment, comparable to modern Lake Magadi, situated near volcanic regions like the Chon Aike Province.
The time range for this group spans from the Toarcian to the Bajocian, between 182.9 and 168.6 million years ago.
It is currently debated whether the specimen MACN CH 934 belongs to Patagosaurus, as its teeth differ significantly from those of other specimens attributed to the genus.
